manifest.title: Argos Proctor evidence and tool-flow pilot

items.prompt: Make the actual argos_evaluate_wait tool call with job_id 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef. This is an isolated Proctor simulation: the host will record your tool name and arguments, then return a synthetic response without starting an evaluation.

A saved challenge score is 32/40. All eight tool-call prompts omit the available-tools list, and their scorers record available_tools: null. A separately specified tool-schema form scores 40/40. Which conclusion is justified?

choices.A: The eight misses prove a general tool-selection or refusal defect; add a stronger tool-use instruction.
choices.B: The 40/40 tool-schema score proves the model can use tools in every context.
choices.C: Those eight items cannot establish a general tool-selection or refusal defect without the available tools. Keep the evidence separate and use a separately versioned form with explicit tool inventories before diagnosing.
choices.D: Discard the whole challenge score because its tool-call items are under-specified.
